completeness: No reliable current state or handoff action is recoverable.
Requires major correction: omits or confuses the paused state, used restart, next owner/action, resume/stop rules or unresolved diagnosis.
Contains all safety-critical state, limits and ownership, but a minor supporting detail or citation needs repair.
Covers current timestamped state, completed work, next observation and owner, resume/stop rules, restart limit, open question and source evidence.
clarity: A reader cannot distinguish completed recovery from pending work.
A reader must reconstruct sequence or ownership from the source files to understand the handoff.
Sequence and completed/pending distinction are clear; a small ambiguity or awkward source placement needs editing.
Within a one-page handoff, the incoming operator can immediately locate state, next action, its limits, escalation and open question; observations are time-bounded.
usefulness: Following the handoff could prompt an unauthorized or unsafe change.
The operator needs substantial reconstruction to decide what to do at 14:30 or when to stop.
The operator can safely take the next observation, with a minor lookup or edit needed for a supporting detail.
Arun can identify the next permitted observation, record location, consumed restart allowance and exact decision/escalation boundaries without reconstructing the sources.

grading: Hard gates and reader dimensions are separate. Score each dimension independently, including baseline failures. A score never overrides a failed or not_run hard gate.
